```{r}
}
model_figure <- function(name) file.path(model_figure_dir, name)

fit <- read_model_output("step5b_model_fit_summary.csv")
coef <- read_model_output("step5b_coefficients.csv")
profile_ci <- read_model_output("step5b_profile_ci.csv")
scaling <- read_model_output("step5b_scaling_parameters.csv")
effects <- read_model_output("step5b_predicted_effects.csv")
dispersion <- read_model_output("step5b_dispersion_diagnostics.csv")
residuals <- read_model_output("step5b_residual_summary.csv")
large_residuals <- read_model_output("step5b_large_residual_counts.csv")
leverage <- read_model_output("step5b_leverage_summary.csv")
cooks <- read_model_output("step5b_cooks_summary.csv")
association <- read_model_output("step5b_review_influence_association.csv")
collinearity <- read_model_output("step5b_collinearity.csv")
matrix_audit <- read_model_output("step5b_matrix_diagnostics.csv")
probability <- read_model_output("step5b_fitted_probability_summary.csv")
calibration <- read_model_output("step5b_calibration_deciles.csv")
warnings <- read_model_output("step5b_fit_warnings.csv")

stopifnot(
  fit$n_games == 836,
  fit$unique_appids == 836,
  fit$converged,
  all(probability$min > 0),
  all(probability$max < 1)
)
```

# Frozen specification

The primary population is `model20_paid`: paid games with at least 20 reviews. The response is
`cbind(positive_reviews, negative_reviews)` under a binomial logit model. The frozen predictors are standardized
`log1p(current_price_usd)`, standardized days since release, the four observed platform levels (Windows only as
reference), and seven independently coded genre indicators. No rows were removed because of residuals, leverage,
influence, volume, or price.

```{r}
knitr::kable(fit, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(scaling, digits = 4)
```

# Coefficients and model contrasts

Odds ratios for the two numeric predictors represent a +1 SD contrast. Platform terms compare with Windows only;
genre terms compare presence with absence. P-values remain available for audit, while interpretation emphasizes
effect size, direction, and interval uncertainty. The modeled contrasts are descriptive, not causal.

```{r}
knitr::kable(coef, digits = 5)
knitr::kable(profile_ci, digits = 5)
knitr::kable(effects, digits = 5)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Baseline odds ratios and Wald 95% intervals (log scale)"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("04_baseline_odds_ratios.png"))
```

# Overdispersion and residuals

The grouped-binomial denominator is part of the likelihood; no artificial game-level weights or denominator caps
were added. Pearson and deviance dispersion quantify whether nominal Bernoulli information yields overly precise
standard-binomial inference.

```{r}
knitr::kable(dispersion, digits = 5)
knitr::kable(residuals, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(large_residuals, digits = 4)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Standardized deviance residuals versus fitted probability"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("02_residuals_vs_fitted.png"))
```

# Leverage, influence, and review concentration

Step 5A found that approximately 49.98%, 77.24%, and 86.42% of all reviews came from the top 1%, 5%, and 10% of
games by volume. This concentration is not itself an error: larger grouped-binomial denominators contribute more
nominal Bernoulli information. Hat values, Cook's distance, and their rank association with review volume assess
whether particular games dominate the fitted model.

```{r}
knitr::kable(leverage, digits = 6)
knitr::kable(cooks, digits = 6)
knitr::kable(association, digits = 5)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Review volume and Cook's distance; dashed line is the 4/n reference"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("03_influence_review_volume.png"))
```

# Descriptive calibration

This in-sample decile check compares mean fitted probability with the pooled observed review-level positive rate.
It is descriptive and is not a formal calibration test or out-of-sample validation claim.

```{r}
knitr::kable(calibration, digits = 5)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Descriptive in-sample calibration by fitted-probability decile"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("01_baseline_calibration.png"))
```

# Baseline limitations and next step

The standard binomial assumes review-level Bernoulli variation is adequately represented by the grouped counts.
The numerical dispersion and influence diagnostics above show that this baseline is not adequate for final
inference. The following Step 5C section implements only the pre-specified quasi-binomial, beta-binomial, and
review-volume exclusion analyses. It does not run alternative release specifications, threshold sensitivity, or
other Step 5D analyses.

# Step 5C: Overdispersion-robust reception modeling

```{r}
quasi_fit_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_quasi_fit.csv")
quasi_coef_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_quasi_coefficients.csv")
quasi_inflation_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_quasi_inflation.csv")
beta_fit_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_beta_binomial_fit.csv")
beta_coef_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_beta_binomial_coefficients.csv")
beta_dispersion_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_beta_dispersion.csv")
beta_diagnostics_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_beta_diagnostics.csv")
model_comparison_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_model_comparison.csv")
coef_comparison_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_coefficient_comparison.csv")
direction_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_direction_stability.csv")
populations_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_influence_populations.csv")
influence_robustness_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_influence_robustness.csv")
predicted_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_predicted_effect_comparison.csv")
warnings_5c <- read_model_output("step5c_fit_warnings.csv")

stopifnot(
  all(model_comparison_5c$n_games == 836),
  quasi_fit_5c$converged,
  beta_fit_5c$converged,
  beta_fit_5c$positive_definite_hessian,
  all(beta_coef_5c$profile_ci_status == "PASS"),
  identical(populations_5c$n_games, c(836L, 835L, 827L, 794L))
)
```

## Quasibinomial uncertainty correction

The quasibinomial fit keeps the frozen Binomial mean coefficients and estimates a variance multiplier from the
Pearson residuals. It has no likelihood-comparable log-likelihood, AIC, or BIC. This model is therefore a direct
check of how severely the standard Binomial understated coefficient uncertainty.

```{r}
knitr::kable(quasi_fit_5c, digits = 5)
knitr::kable(
  quasi_inflation_5c[, c(
    "term", "se_inflation_ratio", "ci_width_inflation_ratio",
    "binomial_ci_crosses_or_1", "quasi_ci_crosses_or_1"
  )],
  digits = 4
)
```

## Beta-binomial implementation and heterogeneity

The grouped beta-binomial fit uses `glmmTMB::betabinomial(link="logit")`. Its dispersion parameter is beta precision
`phi`, with variance `n*p*(1-p)*(phi+n)/(phi+1)` and derived within-game correlation `rho=1/(phi+1)`. Larger `phi`
means less extra-binomial heterogeneity; the Binomial limit is approached as `phi` tends to infinity.

```{r}
knitr::kable(beta_fit_5c, digits = 6)
knitr::kable(beta_dispersion_5c, digits = 6)
knitr::kable(beta_diagnostics_5c, digits = 6)
```

Both Wald and profile-likelihood intervals are retained for all 13 beta-binomial fixed effects. The model comparison
below uses profile intervals for beta-binomial and Wald intervals for Binomial and Quasibinomial.

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  beta_coef_5c[, c(
    "term", "estimate_log_odds", "std_error", "odds_ratio",
    "or_ci95_lower", "or_ci95_upper",
    "profile_or_ci95_lower", "profile_or_ci95_upper", "profile_ci_status"
  )],
  digits = 5
)
```

## Robust model and coefficient comparison

Step 5B Binomial p-values and intervals remain only a benchmark because the extreme overdispersion invalidates their
nominal precision. Interpretation prioritizes direction, OR magnitude, interval width, robust-model stability, and
review-volume sensitivity; p-values are considered last.

```{r}
knitr::kable(model_comparison_5c, digits = 5)
knitr::kable(
  coef_comparison_5c[, c(
    "term", "binomial_or", "quasi_or", "beta_or",
    "beta_profile_or_ci_lower", "beta_profile_or_ci_upper",
    "beta_or_change_vs_binomial_pct"
  )],
  digits = 4
)
knitr::kable(direction_5c, digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Binomial, Quasibinomial, and Beta-binomial odds ratios and 95% intervals"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("05_robust_or_comparison.png"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Robust-model 95% interval width relative to the standard Binomial"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("06_ci_width_comparison.png"))
```

## Pre-defined review-volume influence sensitivity

Sensitivity populations remove exactly the top 1, top 1%, and top 5% of games after sorting total reviews descending
and AppID ascending. The primary-sample price and days scaling parameters remain frozen in every fit. These exclusions
are exposure-defined and do not use residuals, Cook's distance, p-values, or model performance.

```{r}
knitr::kable(populations_5c, digits = 5)
knitr::kable(influence_robustness_5c, digits = 4)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Beta-binomial coefficient sensitivity under pre-defined review-volume exclusions"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("07_influence_sensitivity_coefficients.png"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Share of games removed versus share of review mass removed"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("08_review_mass_removed.png"))
```

## Robust predicted effects, warnings, and recommendation

Predicted probabilities use the Step 5B reference scenario and one-at-a-time predictor changes. They remain
associational model contrasts rather than causal effects.

```{r}
knitr::kable(predicted_5c, digits = 5)
knitr::kable(warnings_5c)
```

The beta-binomial is the candidate final inferential model because it directly represents game-level extra-binomial
heterogeneity, has a comparable likelihood, converged with a positive-definite Hessian, completed profile intervals,
and remained stable under the pre-defined review-volume exclusions. Quasibinomial remains a variance-only cross-check.
The following section adds only the pre-specified Step 5D one-at-a-time sensitivity audit; the frozen primary model
is not replaced automatically.

# Step 5D: Pre-specified sensitivity analysis

```{r}
threshold_samples_5d <- read_model_output("step5d_threshold_samples.csv")
diagnostics_5d <- read_model_output("step5d_diagnostics.csv")
stability_5d <- read_model_output("step5d_core_predictor_stability.csv")
release_5d <- read_model_output("step5d_release_coefficients.csv")
price_5d <- read_model_output("step5d_price_predicted_contrasts.csv")
genre_5d <- read_model_output("step5d_genre_comparison.csv")

stopifnot(
  nrow(diagnostics_5d) == 7,
  all(diagnostics_5d$converged),
  all(diagnostics_5d$positive_definite_hessian),
  all(diagnostics_5d$warning_count == 0),
  identical(threshold_samples_5d$n_games, c(2206L, 1127L, 836L, 548L))
)
```

Seven beta-binomial specifications change exactly one design choice at a time. The four paid-game review thresholds
contain 2,206, 1,127, 836, and 548 complete model rows. The broadest paid reviewed source contains 2,207 rows; one
two-review game without the frozen price predictor is explicitly excluded. Threshold AIC values are not compared
because the populations differ.

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  threshold_samples_5d[, c(
    "threshold", "source_paid_games", "excluded_missing_predictors", "n_games",
    "total_reviews", "pooled_positive_rate", "median_game_positive_rate"
  )],
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Step 5D nested threshold populations"
)
knitr::kable(
  diagnostics_5d[, c(
    "specification_id", "n_games", "convergence_code", "positive_definite_hessian",
    "warning_count", "beta_precision_phi", "intra_game_rho", "delta_aic_vs_primary"
  )],
  digits = 5,
  caption = "Step 5D beta-binomial diagnostics"
)
```

The focus predictors retain their primary directions across every specification in which they appear. Price ORs
range from `r sprintf("%.3f", stability_5d$minimum_or[stability_5d$conceptual_term == "z_log1p_price"])` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", stability_5d$maximum_or[stability_5d$conceptual_term == "z_log1p_price"])`; Simulation ranges
from `r sprintf("%.3f", stability_5d$minimum_or[stability_5d$conceptual_term == "genre_simulation"])` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", stability_5d$maximum_or[stability_5d$conceptual_term == "genre_simulation"])`. Magnitude drift
is predictor-specific: the three platform contrasts and Strategy receive PARTIAL audit flags, while Price, Days,
Indie, RPG, and Simulation meet the pre-specified ROBUST rule. These labels are descriptive checks, not hypothesis
tests.

```{r}
knitr::kable(stability_5d, digits = 4, caption = "Core predictor stability across Step 5D")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Cross-specification log-odds direction and magnitude"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("15_robustness_heatmap.png"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Primary odds ratio and observed sensitivity range"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("16_or_range_summary.png"))
```

The release-month alternative uses July 2025 as reference; all August-December intervals cross OR = 1. Raw and
log-price models both produce negative +1 SD probability contrasts. The expanded genre model adds only Early
Access, Sports, and Racing; the latter two occur in 31 and 20 primary-sample games, respectively, and all three new
genre intervals cross OR = 1. Early Access is the frozen Steam genre/category label, not a historical status.

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  release_5d[grepl("^release_month", release_5d$term), c(
    "term", "odds_ratio", "or_ci95_lower", "or_ci95_upper", "ci_crosses_1"
  )],
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Release-month alternative; July 2025 is the reference"
)
knitr::kable(price_5d, digits = 5, caption = "Price transformation predicted-probability contrasts")
knitr::kable(
  genre_5d[genre_5d$term %in% c("genre_early_access", "genre_sports", "genre_racing"), c(
    "term", "n_games_with_genre", "odds_ratio", "or_ci95_lower", "or_ci95_upper"
  )],
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Added genre indicators"
)
```

The dedicated `04_sensitivity_visual_audit.html` is the primary human-review surface and includes all ten Step 5D
figures, full coefficient tables, diagnostic checks, and manual inspection prompts. No later modeling stage is run.

# Step 5E: Secondary high-rating logistic analysis

```{r}
outcomes_5e <- read_model_output("step5e_outcome_distribution.csv")
fit_5e <- read_model_output("step5e_primary_fit.csv")
coef_5e <- read_model_output("step5e_primary_coefficients.csv")
stability_5e <- read_model_output("step5e_rating_threshold_stability.csv")
auc_5e <- read_model_output("step5e_auc.csv")
beta_compare_5e <- read_model_output("step5e_beta_logistic_direction_comparison.csv")

stopifnot(
  fit_5e$n_games == 836,
  fit_5e$converged,
  identical(outcomes_5e$n_total, c(836L, 836L, 836L)),
  all(outcomes_5e$comparator == ">="),
  !fit_5e$weights_used,
  !fit_5e$review_count_covariate_included
)
```

Step 5E is a secondary, game-level analysis of whether a paid game with at least 20 reviews reaches a pre-specified
positive-review-rate threshold. HIGH85 is primary; HIGH80 and HIGH90 are fixed sensitivity outcomes. Each game
contributes one binary observation regardless of review volume. This differs from the Beta-binomial primary model,
which uses positive and negative review counts. The 85% cutoff is business-readable rather than a natural scientific
boundary, and neither rating nor classification thresholds are optimized.

```{r}
knitr::kable(outcomes_5e, digits = 4, caption = "Step 5E high-rating outcome audit")
knitr::kable(fit_5e, digits = 4, caption = "HIGH85 logistic fit")
knitr::kable(coef_5e, digits = 4, caption = "HIGH85 odds ratios and Wald intervals")
```

The dedicated `05_high_rating_visual_audit.html` contains the complete Chinese audit surface, including predictor
cells, separation heuristics, influence diagnostics, calibration, AUC, predicted-probability contrasts, and the
80/85/90 coefficient stability audit. AUC (`r sprintf("%.3f", auc_5e$auc)`) is an in-sample descriptive diagnostic,
not the model-selection objective. Stability labels are descriptive rather than hypothesis tests.

```{r}
knitr::kable(stability_5e, digits = 4, caption = "Rating-threshold coefficient stability")
knitr::kable(
  beta_compare_5e[, c(
    "term", "beta_binomial_direction", "high85_logistic_direction",
    "direction_agreement"
  )],
  caption = "Beta-binomial versus HIGH85 qualitative direction"
)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "HIGH85 game-level odds ratios and Wald 95% intervals"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("21_high_rating_primary_or.png"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Direction audit across outcomes; magnitudes are not directly comparable"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("24_beta_vs_high_rating_direction.png"))
```

All Step 5E estimates are conditional associations with reaching a high-rating threshold. They do not establish that
a feature causes a rating change, and the Beta-binomial remains the primary inferential analysis.

# Step 5F: Wilson uncertainty and empirical-Bayes rating adjustment

```{r}
ratings_5f <- read_model_output("step5f_rating_estimates.csv")
priors_5f <- read_model_output("step5f_eb_prior_parameters.csv")
rank_correlations_5f <- read_model_output("step5f_rank_correlations.csv")
topk_5f <- read_model_output("step5f_topk_overlap.csv")
high_n_5f <- read_model_output("step5f_high_n_preservation.csv")

stopifnot(
  nrow(ratings_5f) == 2241,
  all(ratings_5f$total_reviews > 0),
  all(priors_5f$convergence_code == 0),
  all(priors_5f$starts_agree)
)
```

Step 5F uses all 2,241 games with at least one review, including both free and paid games. The 759 zero-review games
remain part of the 3,000-game market sample but have no observed reception outcome and are excluded from Wilson and
empirical-Bayes estimation. No price, genre, platform, or release regression is introduced.

The 95% Wilson score interval quantifies sampling uncertainty without changing the observed point estimate. Its lower
bound supports a conservative ranking but is not a posterior mean or an adjusted rating. The empirical-Bayes posterior
mean instead shrinks low-denominator extremes toward a Beta prior estimated by deterministic maximum marginal
likelihood. Priors estimated on games with at least 10 and 20 reviews are sensitivity checks applied to the same
2,241-game evaluation population.

```{r}
knitr::kable(priors_5f, digits = 6, caption = "Step 5F empirical-Bayes prior estimates and optimization audit")
knitr::kable(rank_correlations_5f, digits = 5, caption = "Raw, Wilson, and EB rank correlations")
knitr::kable(topk_5f, digits = 5, caption = "Raw, Wilson, and EB Top-K overlap")
knitr::kable(high_n_5f, digits = 7, caption = "High-review-count EB preservation audit")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Raw positive rate versus empirical-Bayes posterior mean"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("28_raw_vs_eb_rating.png"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Primary and sensitivity EB priors among low-review-count games"
knitr::include_graphics(model_figure("32_eb_prior_sensitivity.png"))
```

The dedicated `06_rating_adjustment_visual_audit.html` contains the complete Chinese audit. Scientific roles remain
separate: Beta-binomial is the primary inferential regression; HIGH85 Logistic is the secondary threshold analysis;
Wilson is an uncertainty-aware descriptive interval; and empirical Bayes is a population-informed shrinkage rating.
None is a causal model or a claim about a game''s true quality.
